bio: Richard Juien-Dah Pan (born October 28, 1965) is an American Democratic politician and physician who served in the California State Senate from 2014 to 2022, representing the 6th Senate district, which encompassed parts of Sacramento and Yolo counties. He is a practicing pediatrician and professor at the University of California, Davis. He is the U.S. representative-elect for California's 6th congressional district, having defeated incumbent Kevin Kiley in the 2026 election.
offices: Member of the State Senate of California (2014–2022)
Member of the California State Assembly (2010–2014)

items.t: Co-introduced Senate Bill 277 (2015), which eliminated philosophical and religious belief exemptions to vaccine requirements for California school children; it was signed into law.
items.q: Pan and Senator Ben Allen introduced California Senate Bill 277 in 2015, which eliminated philosophical and religious beliefs exemptions to vaccine requirements for California school children.

items.t: Authored laws expanding newborn screening, including AB395 (2011), AB1559 (2014) and SB1095 (2016).
items.q: Pan authored laws to expand newborn screening for severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (AB395 in 2011), adrenoleukodystrophy (AB1559 in 2014)

items.t: Authored legislation to extend the California Children's Services Program managed care carve-out (AB301, 2011).

items.t: Co-introduced Senate Bill 866 (2022), which would have allowed minors aged 15 and older to consent to FDA-approved vaccinations; it did not become law.
items.q: Pan introduced Senate Bill 866, ⟦13⟧ which would have allowed minors aged 15 and older to give consent to receive FDA-approved vaccinations for themselves.
